summary: The re-base rule: merge_one returns 3 when main moved; the lane (or a LANE_MERGE merge lane, coordinator or harness merge) merges main into the verified commit; disjoint files: full suite, tag forced to the merged commit, merge; overlapping or LANE_REBASE=verify: one verify round. Review's 5 findings fixed. Suite 566 -> 574, green.
verified_how: tests/checks/48-lanes-rebase.sh 8/8: rb (disjoint: note, uncached check: green in lanes/M2/rebase-check.out, merged, git -C origin.git diff --quiet run/rb/M2 main, origin reflog shows only refs/tags/run/rb/M2 rewritten), ro (overlapping (shared.txt), two verify M2 sessions, 're-base verify round 1 of 1' in its prompt), rv (LANE_REBASE=verify), rr (MAX_REBASE_ROUNDS=0 needs Michael), rf (failed round removes tag; watched red with the fix disabled), rp (MERGE_POLICY=pr, harness merge re-bases M1 then M2). Full suite via check.sh: green, 574 tests, 437 s. bash -n on every touched shell file.

dead_ends.tried: reading the origin's reflog after resetting main between runs
dead_ends.why: update-ref of main is itself a logged non-fast-forward; the rewritten refs are now read before the reset

discoveries.text: merge_milestones_ now skips a milestone whose lane is alive (other than the caller's own, by pid == $$): the coordinator's reap never merges a lane's milestone under it; lane_alive moved from driver.sh to record.sh

A re-base verify round that fails removes verified-<m> and the tag run/<run>/<m> locally and on origin (else the old tag would merge or block a later tag -a); lane_done checks needs-<m> before waits-<m> (waits-<m> is never cleared)
48-lanes-rebase.sh costs ~77 s of slot time (six stub runs); each run resets origin main with update-ref so the stub's work files are new
harness merge clears moved-* (one more re-base per main); harness continue also clears rebase-rounds-* and moved-*; harness merge clears a stale lanes-end before its merge lanes
